caption: We argued about the takeaways number for a full evening. How much do you two actually spend?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R47 000
household income
Living in Johannesburg
slides.body:
Him 34, her 31
Married, one toddler
Jobs: Fleet controller & school administrator
Combined net: R47 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.includes: 3 bed townhouse in Roodepoort, 19 years left
slides.body: We bought at the top of the rate cycle. Every drop takes months to show up here.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers, Makro run once a month, nappies
slides.body: Two adults and a two year old. The nappies alone are R700 of this.

slides.title: Car instalments
slides.includes: His bakkie R3 900, her Polo R2 300
slides.body: Two cars in one house feels ridiculous until you look at where we both work.

slides.title: Petrol & insurance
slides.includes: Petrol R2 900, insurance on both cars R1 400
slides.body: He does Roodepoort to Isando daily. That drive is most of this number.

slides.title: Takeaways & delivery
slides.includes: Weeknight delivery, Sunday KFC, work lunches
slides.body: We told each other it was maybe R1 200. It is R2 800. Both of us were wrong and neither of us was surprised.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Creche, medical aid, rates & levies, electricity, phone & fibre, black tax, funeral policies, stokvel
slides.body: None of these felt big on their own. Together they're R15 900 and we have never once sat down and discussed them.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R47 000. That is about R33 a day between two adults, and we still call ourselves the responsible ones.

slides.title: We stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

It found four delivery orders in one week we both swore never happened.

No bank login needed.
